﻿Thermal Storage


* Thermal Energy Storage
Thermal Energy Storage (TES) is a technology that stores heat for later use. It can store heat produced by solar thermal systems, electric heaters, waste heat, steam or other heat sources and supply that heat when the MSME needs it, including when the original heat source is unavailable.
Field
	Value
	Process
	Stores and supplies heat for hot-water generation, steam generation, drying, heating, pre-heating and other industrial processes
	Temperature
	Typically ~50–300°C for many industrial TES applications; depends on the storage material and system design
	Energy source
	Solar thermal, electric heating, waste heat, steam or other heat sources
	Efficiency
	Typically ~70–95% thermal storage/recovery efficiency, depending on storage technology, insulation and operating temperature
	CAPEX
	Highly technology- and capacity-dependent; roughly ₹10,000–₹40,000/kWhₜₕ for many small/medium thermal-storage systems as a planning range
	OPEX
	Low — mainly insulation inspection, pumps/valves, heat-transfer-fluid maintenance and control-system maintenance
	Lifetime
	Typically 15–25+ years, depending on storage material, operating temperature and system design
	Space
	Moderate — requires an insulated tank, vessel or storage unit; space increases with required storage capacity
	Constraints
	Heat losses during storage, storage-material limitations, space requirement, insulation quality, operating temperature and correct sizing
	Additional important points
Field
	Value
	Existing equipment it can replace/reduce
	Reduces the need for additional boiler/heater operation during periods when the primary heat source is unavailable
	Maintenance required
	Insulation inspection, tank/vessel inspection, pump and valve maintenance, temperature monitoring and heat-transfer-fluid checks where applicable
	Backup required?
	Not necessarily, but a backup boiler/heater is recommended for critical continuous industrial processes
	Thermal storage
	This technology itself is thermal storage — it stores heat for later use
	Emissions reduction
	Can reduce CO₂ and fuel consumption by allowing renewable or waste heat to be stored and used later
	Best suited for
	Indian MSMEs with variable heat demand, especially those using solar thermal, waste heat or electric heating and needing heat after the heat source is unavailable
	In the same simple style:
Thermal Energy Storage is a heat-storage technology that stores heat produced by solar thermal systems, electric heaters, waste heat or other sources and releases it later when the MSME needs it. It helps match heat supply with demand and can reduce the need for fossil-fuel backup during periods when renewable or low-cost heat is unavailable.
MSME optimizer
The basic flow is:
Heat source → Thermal Storage → Process
For example:
Solar thermal → TES → Evening process heat
Electric heater during low-tariff hours → TES → Process during high-tariff hours
For your Indian MSME project, Sensible Heat Storage is the simplest and most practical category to prioritize, especially for hot-water and low/medium-temperature applications.
